runs.text: The factorial is part of the EGF convention; [x^n] alone returns a_n/n!.
EGFs are suited to structures on labeled n-element sets. Their product automatically records the choice of which labels go to each component.
Addition encodes disjoint alternatives. Multiplication combines labeled components; the binomial coefficient chooses the labels assigned to the first component.

items.text: Do not read the coefficient of x^n as a_n; multiply it by n!.
The labeled-product interpretation requires disjoint label sets whose union is the full set.
Differentiation shifts the indexed sequence by one without an extra n factor because of factorial normalization.
Formal power-series reasoning and analytic convergence are separate issues here as with OGFs.

items.text: Using an OGF product for labeled components omits the binomial choice of labels.
Using an EGF does not itself prove a construction is labeled or disjoint; the combinatorial model still matters.
Do not lose the constant term when differentiating, integrating, or imposing initial values.
